sector_model: software/SaaS supply-chain network: P/E GAAP and non-GAAP, FCF yield after SBC, EV/sales, EBITDA margin, net cash, buyback cover
thesis: SPS Commerce (Nasdaq: SPSC) runs a cloud retail supply-chain network (EDI/fulfillment, analytics) with no debt. Q3 2026 (ended 2026-09-30): revenue 197.6M (+4%), GAAP NI 30.7M ($0.85 vs $0.67), non-GAAP EPS $1.39 (vs $1.13), adjusted EBITDA 70.9M (36% margin vs 32%). Nine-month revenue 587.6M (+5%); nine-month GAAP NI 57.3M (vs 67.5M) after a 23.5M loss on the 2026-06-30 sale of the 3P revenue recovery business. FY26 guidance: revenue 786.9-788.9M (~+5%), non-GAAP EPS 5.05-5.11, adjusted EBITDA margin ~34%. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 153.8M plus short-term investments 29.7M, no debt shown, total liabilities 199.7M, equity 932.9M. TTM OCF 231.5M less capex 28.9M = FCF 202.6M; SBC 62.9M TTM so FCF after SBC 139.8M. Close 82.25 (2026-11-12): market cap about 2.92B on 35.44M shares, EV about 2.73B, EV/TTM sales 3.5x, FCF yield 7.0% (4.8% after SBC), 35x TTM GAAP EPS (about 27x ignoring the 23.5M divestiture loss), 16x FY26 non-GAAP EPS guidance. Nine-month buybacks 147.2M (about 79% of OCF). Possibly cheap versus its own history (52-week range 49.04-96.54, now mid-range) if growth holds, but growth is only mid single digit and the cheap-looking non-GAAP multiple excludes about 1.7 dollars per share of SBC; no clear mispricing proven.
counterthesis: Revenue growth has slowed to 4-5% (recurring +4%, customer count -15% largely from the divestiture); a mid-single-digit grower with 62.9M TTM SBC (8% of sales) is not obviously cheap at 4.8% FCF yield after SBC and 27-35x GAAP earnings. Non-GAAP EPS of 5.08 excludes SBC and amortization, so the 16x multiple is flattered. Margin gains in 2026 partly reflect the divestiture and cost control; Q2 GAAP NI was only 6.9M. Retail customer concentration/tariff-driven volume risk, AI-driven disruption of EDI software, and large buybacks at higher prices than the 2025 low are risks. Peer multiples (descriptions: Descartes, Manhattan, Kinaxis, Appfolio, Paycom) and 10-K risk factors/audit matters were not read; CEO 10b5-1 plan and leadership transition are unassessed.
invalidation: Valuation case would need FCF yield after SBC above about 6% or evidence growth reaccelerates above 8% organically. Quality thesis fails if organic recurring revenue growth falls below 3%, adjusted EBITDA margin drops below 30%, or SBC rises faster than revenue.
